slice: natural explaining: body and germ cells, one society, no war

items.section: 5.5 Multicellularity and the germ-soma split — many selves into one; the self going on and the sharing surface
items.text: A germ line set apart from the body's other cells is a form in many animals and is-not a law of living: in plants, germ cells arise from vegetative meristem cells of the body, possibly many years old, and changes in those body lines can reach the germ line; in sponges and corals, stem cell lineages give both body cells and reproductive cells.

items.section: 5.5 Multicellularity and the germ-soma split — many selves into one; the self going on and the sharing surface
items.text: Body cells and germ cells are one same-existing-society: its germ cells are its going on to its next same-existing-society, and its body cells its sharing surface now-living with that next; reproductive altruism, a body sacrificing, selfish cells policing, a germline a body sequesters and protects, and an arms race between a genome and its retroviruses are a field's story of agents fixing still and competing over a store, and 5.5 says each by bi-moral co-agency within one same-existing-society.

Transcribing, translating, reading, a code and information at a cell are a text-and-machine story over a cell's living: RNA and proteins forming along a genome are the cell's own stable-forming with its artifact, and a cell reads no text and runs no machine.

A self observing a body sees no war within it: body cells and germ cells, a mother and her child, a cell and its retroviral sequences are each a same-existing-society's selves and their artifacts, and a fight, an invasion, an escape and an arms race are a field's equilibria story over them; a cell landing from coupling, reproducing alone against its whole, is cancer at Natural Biology 5.5, a landing and is-not a war.
